our_title: CMake gpart_overlap_2 runs gmtst without -o, reading the overlap map as a plain mapping
ran: cmake 4.4.4 build of base-combined ($W/cm, RelWithDebInfo, shared). ctest -V -R '^gpart_overlap_2$' (pristine): gmtst prints 'M Processors 32/32 (1) ... M Neighbors min=0 max=0 sum=0 ... CommCutSz=0.000000 (0)' and the test Passes. Direct: gmtst data/bump_imbal_32.grf tgt/k32.tgt bump_imbal_32_part_ovl_32.map -> same plain-mapping lines, rc=0; gmtst -o ... -> 'P sep=1201 / P min=385 max=465 avg=421.188 / P maxavg=1.10402 minavg=0.914082', rc=0. Patched: ctest -V shows the 'P sep=' lines, Passed. Full ctest of the patched tree: 100% of 181 tests passed.
severity_note: Lower than the review's medium: the test never asserted anything in either mode (gmtst exits 0 in both); what is lost is only the exercise of the overlap-statistics code path, which gpart_overlap_1 and _4 still cover in CMake.
evidence:
add_test(NAME gpart_overlap_2 COMMAND ${BASH} -c "'$<TARGET_FILE:gpart>' -o 32 '${dat}/bump_imbal_32.grf' bump_imbal_32_part_ovl_32.map -vmt && \
  '$<TARGET_FILE:gmtst>' '${dat}/bump_imbal_32.grf' '${tgt}/k32.tgt' bump_imbal_32_part_ovl_32.map")  vs src/check/Makefile:844: $(SCOTCHBINDIR)/gmtst -o data/bump_imbal_32.grf $(SCOTCHTGTDIR)/k32.tgt ...
review_accuracy: Accurate on the omission; the quoted 'Processors 0/32' output is not what 7.0.17's gpart/gmtst produce here (32/32), but the point stands: the overlap map is read as a plain mapping.
first_pass_critique: Status, location and evidence right; its 'Processors 0/32' line came from a run of a different map; it did not run the CMake test itself (no cmake), which I did.

fix_options.label: Add -o (match the Makefile)
fix_options.summary: Insert -o in the gmtst call of gpart_overlap_2.
fix_options.tested: ctest -V -R gpart_overlap_2 on the patched tree shows the overlap statistics; full ctest 181/181.
fix_options.tradeoffs: One token; no behaviour change elsewhere.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Matches the Makefile line 844 and the two other overlap tests in the same file; the maintainer did exactly this once already (20ac409 'Bugifx: added missing option -o to gmtst command').

fix_options.label: Also assert on the output
fix_options.summary: Pipe gmtst -o into grep -q '^P[[:space:]]*sep=' so the test fails if the overlap statistics are not printed.
fix_options.tested: untested: would need pipefail semantics in the bash -c string; sketch only.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Gives the test teeth but diverges from the Makefile twin and from every other gmtst test in the file.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Not his style: the check suite only checks exit statuses of the tools; he would add a real assertion in gmtst, not in a grep.

notes: Verified with a real cmake (installed as a uv tool into $W/bin); not available system-wide.

our_title: CMake scotchf.h and ptscotchf.h custom commands depend on library.h, not on the Fortran templates
ran: $W/cm (pristine): touch src/libscotch/library_f.h library_pt_f.h; make -C cm/src/libscotch -> scotchf.h regenerated: NO, ptscotchf.h regenerated: NO (generated files in cm/src/include). touch library.h -> '[  3%] Generate scotchf.h' '[  4%] Generate ptscotchf.h' (spurious). Patched: touch library_f.h library_pt_f.h -> both regenerated: yes; touch library.h -> scotch.h yes, scotchf.h NO. Clean build and full ctest of the patched tree OK (181/181).
severity_note: Lower than the review's medium: affects developers editing the Fortran templates (a clean build is always right); no user-visible effect.
evidence:
add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/scotchf.h
  COMMAND $<TARGET_FILE:dummysizes>  "-s${SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX}"
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/library_f.h ${GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/scotchf.h DEPENDS dummysizes
  DEPENDS library.h   /   ... library_pt_f.h ${GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/ptscotchf.h DEPENDS ptdummysizes
    DEPENDS library.h
first_pass_critique: Right but source-read only (no cmake); I ran it. Its option 2 (depend on both) is unnecessary: the sizes dummysizes embeds come from the compiled dummysizes target, already a dependency, not from library.h.

our_title: Sonar token expanded into sonar-project.properties, archived for 15 days with the -X scanner log
read_only: everything: no CI secret was used and no scanner run; only the script and job text were read
why_not_run: running the job needs the GitLab runner, the Sonar server and the real token; none of that is wanted here
severity_note: Agrees with the review: a credential in a downloadable artifact; mitigated only by the schedule-only rule and the project's artifact permissions.
evidence: cat > sonar-project.properties << EOF\nsonar.host.url=https://sonarqube.inria.fr/sonarqube\nsonar.login=$SONARQUBE_LOGIN  /  script: - sonar-scanner -X > sonar.log ; artifacts: paths: - analyzer_reports - sonar-project.properties - ./*.log ... expire_in: 15 days
review_accuracy: Accurate. sonar.login is also deprecated (SonarQube 10) in favour of sonar.token / SONAR_TOKEN.
first_pass_critique: Right. Its preferred sketch exported SONAR_TOKEN in the script; the patch sets it with the job's variables: block (no shell line, no echo) and also stops archiving ./*.log, which its sketch kept.

fix_options.label: Token through SONAR_TOKEN, nothing archived
fix_options.summary: Drop sonar.login from the heredoc; variables: SONAR_TOKEN: $SONARQUBE_LOGIN; run sonar-scanner without -X and without redirection; archive neither the properties file nor logs.
fix_options.tested: YAML parsed with pyyaml (job keys as intended); no scanner run.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Needs a SonarScanner CLI that reads SONAR_TOKEN (4.7+); output goes to the job trace, which GitLab masks; -X debug output lost (re-add it when debugging, it stays in the trace).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Smallest change that removes the secret from disk and artifacts; same shape as his CI edits (variables blocks per job).

fix_options.label: -Dsonar.token on the command line
fix_options.summary: sonar-scanner -Dsonar.token="$SONARQUBE_LOGIN"; drop the file and logs from artifacts.
fix_options.tested: untested
fix_options.tradeoffs: Works with any scanner version, but the token is visible in the runner's process list.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Acceptable fallback if the runner's scanner is older than 4.7.

fix_options.label: Keep the file, stop archiving it
fix_options.summary: Leave analysis.sh; remove sonar-project.properties and ./*.log from artifacts; drop -X.
fix_options.tested: untested
fix_options.tradeoffs: Token still written to the runner workspace; one artifacts glob away from leaking again.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Half a fix.

cleanup_done: removed the sonar.log redirection and the two artifact paths that carried the secret
needs_note: The token already archived in past pipelines must be rotated by the project owners; not a code change.
notes: Never printed or copied any token value; the heredoc line was deleted, not edited.

our_title: JOB_INT=64 adds no flags and CMake jobs never set INTSIZE, IDXSIZE, suffix or determinism
ran: JOB_INT=64-64 bash -c 'source ci/env_makefile.sh' -> '-O0 -g -fPIC -DINTSIZE64 -DIDXSIZE64 -DSCOTCH_MPI_ASYNC_COLL'. The new build_cmake_gcc_64 options were run locally on the series ($W/cm64: cmake -DINTSIZE=64 -DIDXSIZE=64 -DSCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX=_64 -DSCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC=FULL; make -j4; ctest -j4): the first run failed to build (Fortran test unsuffixed: PS2-G30-4; test_scotch_arch_build.c without module.h: PS2-G30-6), both fixed in patches 0011/0012; final result: 100% of 179 tests passed (cm64 ctest rc=0, build warnings: only the pre-existing test_scotch_graph_induce.c memset one). 64-bit Makefile tree (-DINTSIZE64 -DIDXSIZE64, ASan): check/ptcheck/escheck as in BLD-11 notes. YAML validated with pyyaml.
read_only: the runner architectures behind the 32bits/64bits tags and the pipeline itself (GitLab not reachable)
evidence: 64 )\n       export JOBBUILDFLAGS="${JOBBUILDFLAGS}" ;;   /  .matrix_64: JOB_INT: [64] only  /  cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON .. || fatal
review_accuracy: Accurate; its 'only exercised on 32-bit runners' reading of the tags is the natural one but cannot be verified from the repository.
first_pass_critique: Its preferred option redefines JOB_INT=64 to mean INTSIZE64, which would silently drop the only rows that test the default int on 64-bit hosts (the common packaged configuration); the naming already encodes host-int as '32-64', so '64-64' is the consistent addition. It did not try the CMake options, which immediately expose two build breaks under a suffix.

fix_options.label: Add 64-64 rows and a non-default CMake job
fix_options.summary: env_makefile.sh: 64-64 adds -DINTSIZE64 -DIDXSIZE64; matrix_64 gets [64, 64-64] plain and a 64-64/m/d/a row; build_cmake.sh honours JOB_CMAKE_FLAGS; new build_cmake_gcc_64/test_cmake_gcc_64 jobs with INTSIZE=64 IDXSIZE=64 SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX=_64 SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC=FULL.
fix_options.tested: Local runs above; YAML parse.
fix_options.tradeoffs: +3 Makefile jobs and +2 CMake jobs of CI time; the CMake job needs patches 0011 and 0012 (and G29's suffix work, if any) to be green.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same shape as cbd825d ('Added testing of 32bit build with -DINTSIZE64': a new row, not a redefinition) and 0095b91 (matrix rows added per flag); the per-compiler CMake jobs are extended with one more explicit pair, as 31825e9 did.

fix_options.label: Redefine JOB_INT=64 as INTSIZE64 (the review's fix)
fix_options.summary: case 64) adds -DINTSIZE64 -DIDXSIZE64.
fix_options.tested: untested
fix_options.tradeoffs: No new jobs, but the default-int/64-bit-host configuration is no longer tested at all.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Loses coverage he explicitly built the matrix for.

needs_note: The GitLab pipeline must be run once by the maintainers. G29's ci/check_sources.sh (its patch 0005) is wired into ci/build_cmake.sh by this series' patch 0010 ('./ci/check_sources.sh || fatal' before mkdir -p build): patch 0010 therefore needs G29's 0005 to be merged too, else the CMake build jobs fail on the missing script.
notes: The CMake job found two real suffix breaks (PS2-G30-4, PS2-G30-6), which is the point of BLD-14; both are fixed in this series so that the job is green. G29's PS2-G29-4 is the same defect as PS2-G30-4 (fixed by 0011).
